answer: A practical defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, costly-to-repeat bond: it locks a deposit, then earns reputation only when independent peers verify useful work over time. A sybil can create many names, but each must tie up capital and survive the same audits; coordinated accounts that endorse one another do not count as independent signal. Slashing deposits for proven fraud makes attacks expensive, while gradual trust limits the damage from fresh identities. A pearl-sized reward is not worth risking a basalt-sized bond.
